name: Moscow
summary: First mentioned in 1147, Moscow rose from a small fort on the Moskva River to the heart of Russia. Its princes gathered power under Mongol overlordship, then threw it off; Ivan the Terrible was crowned the first tsar here in 1547 beneath the new domes of St Basil's. Peter the Great moved the capital to St Petersburg in 1712, but the Bolsheviks brought it back in 1918, and from the Kremlin Lenin and Stalin ruled the Soviet Union. Burned by Napoleon, besieged by Hitler, it endures as Europe's largest city.

events.title: First mention
events.body: Moscow is first recorded when Prince Yuri Dolgoruky invites an ally to feast here.

events.title: The Mongols burn Moscow
events.body: The Mongol invasion destroys the small wooden town.

events.title: A princely seat
events.body: Moscow becomes the seat of a minor branch of the Rurikid princes.

events.title: Ivan Kalita
events.body: Ivan I gathers wealth and the seat of the Orthodox Church, raising Moscow’s power.

events.title: Kulikovo
events.body: Dmitry Donskoy of Moscow beats a Mongol army at Kulikovo.

events.title: The Mongol yoke ends
events.body: Ivan III ends Mongol overlordship and builds the brick Kremlin that still stands.

events.title: Ivan the Terrible, Tsar
events.body: Ivan IV is crowned the first Tsar of all Russia in Moscow.

events.title: St Basil's Cathedral
events.body: Ivan builds the fantastical St Basil’s on Red Square.

events.title: The Tatars burn Moscow
events.body: A Crimean Tatar raid burns almost the entire city.

events.title: The Time of Troubles
events.body: Muscovites expel a Polish garrison from the Kremlin, ending years of chaos.

events.title: The capital moves away
events.body: Peter the Great moves the capital to St Petersburg; Moscow becomes the second city.

events.title: Moscow University
events.body: Russia’s first university is founded in Moscow.

events.title: Napoleon and the great fire
events.body: Napoleon takes Moscow, but the city burns and his army retreats to ruin.

events.title: The railway to St Petersburg
events.body: The two capitals are linked by rail.

events.title: Revolution
events.body: An armed uprising in Moscow is crushed in the revolution of 1905.

events.title: The Bolsheviks
events.body: Revolution sweeps Russia; fierce fighting takes the Kremlin.

events.title: Capital again
events.body: Lenin moves the capital back to Moscow; the Kremlin becomes the seat of Soviet power.

events.title: The Metro opens
events.body: Moscow’s palatial underground railway opens.

events.title: The Battle of Moscow
events.body: The Red Army halts the Nazi advance at the very gates of the city.

events.title: Stalin dies
events.body: The dictator dies; his long rule from the Kremlin ends.

events.title: The Moscow Olympics
events.body: The USSR hosts the Summer Games, boycotted by much of the West.

events.title: The Soviet collapse
events.body: A failed coup in Moscow hastens the end of the Soviet Union.

events.title: The constitutional crisis
events.body: Tanks shell the Russian parliament in a violent political standoff.

caveats: This timeline is compiled from general reference works — listed under Sources — rather than an event-by-event archive of primary documents, as the Mumbai timeline is. Treat it as a reliable outline, not a citation of record.
Dates for the earliest, legendary events are traditional rather than documented.
